crime.value: A series of poisonings of insect collectors near a New England lake (staged as accidents with their own killing-bottles/snakebite), culminating in the parathion-spray murder of farmer Darrell — the question being whether the deaths were coincidence and who engineered the final killing
crime.quote: "I decided that those four people had been killed, Jim."

victim.value: Four butterfly/beetle collectors killed as 'executions' for cruelty to insects; ultimately Darrell, the wealthy New England farmer, killable because his wife Barbara wanted his farm and $50,000 insurance to return to Manhattan
victim.quote: "The farm plus fifty thousand in insurance was indeed comforting."

closed_world.value: A sequestered, superstition-shunned wooded section at the north end of a lake near a small New England farming town where everyone knows everyone, so a stranger is instantly notable
closed_world.quote: "There were almost no visitors to this sequestered section at the north end of the lake anymore."

culprit_and_motive.value: Jim, a frail Lakeville college professor and fanatical insect-avenger, physically commits the killings; but Barbara, the farmer's wife, is the true culprit — she sought him out and manipulated his mania into murdering her husband for money and freedom
culprit_and_motive.quote: "I know their habits," she said. "I can help... I'll tell you when and where to strike!"

resolution.value: Barbara shoots and wounds Jim, telephones Sheriff Reed, plays the grieving widow; Jim is arrested, found sane, convicted and executed in the gas chamber — 'the killing-bottle' — while Barbara goes free and unsuspected
resolution.quote: "He knew when the cyanide pellets dropped into a bucket of acid under his chair"

investigator.value: No true detective; the reader alternates between the killer Jim and Barbara, the manipulator-amateur sleuth who deduced the pattern of deaths, while Sheriff Reed is explicitly incompetent
investigator.quote: "Our local Sheriff Reed thought it was simply a coincidence. But then he seems to be a very stupid and complaisant fellow."

suspect_architecture.value: Effectively a two-hander rather than a suspect pool: Jim, the frail entomophile professor who murders butterfly collectors out of righteous zeal, and Barbara, the farmer's wife who manipulates him into killing her wealthy husband Darrell. Sheriff Reed serves as the credulous authority; no other candidates are offered.
suspect_architecture.quote: Identification says he's a college professor from over in Lakeville.

red_herring.value: The staged framing of the shed killing as a burglary gone wrong ('Darrell thought it was a robber'), plus the earlier deaths dressed as coincidental accidents from killing-bottle fumes and a snakebite.
red_herring.quote: “Darrell thought it was a robber and went out to see,” she said.

clue_fairness.value: Reader sees everything the sheriff never does: Barbara's daily month-long stakeout to find the killer, her craving to return to Manhattan 'one way or another', her judo skill, and her coaching Jim on when and where to strike.
clue_fairness.quote: “I know their habits,” she said. “I can help. I know when they work and where to find them. I'll tell you when and where to strike!”

social_world.value: Rural New England farm country — superstitious locals, a stereotype of grim tight-lipped wealthy farmers, an incurious small-town sheriff — set against a city actress's dependence on her husband's money and her contempt for the life it bought her.
social_world.quote: it would alleviate the nauseating monotony of being the wife of a farmer. Especially a New England farmer, who happened to be wealthy.

alibi.value: Barbara's alibi is her own performance: she is in the farmhouse, telephones the sheriff, shoots the intruder, and plays the grieving widow — positioning her as victim rather than instigator.
alibi.quote: “I got here quick as I could when you telephoned. But I guess I couldn't have helped much nohow.”

reveal_mechanic.value: Dramatic irony rather than detection: the gas chamber's cyanide fumes mirror the killing-bottle, and Barbara's private accounting of farm plus fifty thousand insurance and a Park Avenue penthouse discloses the true motive to the reader alone.
reveal_mechanic.quote: The farm plus fifty thousand in insurance was indeed comforting.

media_and_audience.value: The killings are publicly packaged as coincidence, then madness: locals blame ghoul-haunted woods, the sheriff calls Jim 'buggy' and a thief, and the court hears an insanity claim Jim himself disclaims — shielding Barbara entirely.
media_and_audience.quote: “He—he must have been crazy or something,” she said thinly.

investigator_wound.value: Sheriff Reed's want of imagination and sentimental deference to a grieving widow — the very complaisance Barbara counts on — is the exploited vulnerability.
investigator_wound.quote: But then he seems to be a very stupid and complaisant fellow. Not much imagination.

victims_enemies.value: Darrell, the wealthy New England farmer, is resented by his wife Barbara, who finds marriage to him nauseating monotony and wants Manhattan money and freedom; he is also, as a user of parathion crop spray, an abstract 'killer of millions' in Jim's moral scheme.
victims_enemies.quote: it would alleviate the nauseating monotony of being the wife of a farmer

suspect_wounds.value: Jim, the frail entomophile college professor, is a self-confessed 'crackpot' whose obsessive love of insects and prior four killings make him instantly and totally guilty-looking; his loneliness and craving for a kindred spirit is the vulnerability Barbara activates.
suspect_wounds.quote: People think I'm abnormal in some way, a kind of—well—a crackpot.

unreliable_frame.value: Barbara's account is wholly false: her professed reverence for 'God's innocent' and her tearful widow's testimony to Sheriff Reed are performance by a former actress; her real aim is insurance money and a Park Avenue penthouse.
unreliable_frame.quote: The farm plus fifty thousand in insurance was indeed comforting. She would sell the farm, rent a penthouse on Park Avenue.

setting_as_constraint.value: The sequestered, 'ghoul-haunted' north-end woods that superstitious locals avoid gives total privacy for meetings and murder; the isolated farm, its pre-dawn storage shed of parathion barrels, and Barbara's insider knowledge of her husband's routine fix exactly when and where the killing can occur.
setting_as_constraint.quote: I know their habits… I know when they work and where to find them. I'll tell you when and where to strike!

evidence_type.value: Testimonial — the widow's eyewitness account plus her shooting and detaining of the intruder; supported by physical identification papers naming him a Lakeville college professor. No evidence ever touches Barbara.
evidence_type.quote: Identification says he's a college professor from over in Lakeville.

false_suspect.value: None functions as an innocent scapegoat; the intended narrative-level dupe is Jim himself, genuinely guilty of the act but framed as a lone lunatic 'robber' to conceal the true instigator, Barbara.
false_suspect.quote: "Darrell thought it was a robber and went out to see," she said.

technical_detail.value: Entomological killing-bottle chemistry: potassium cyanide under cotton wool giving almond-scented, instantly lethal fumes; and parathion, an agricultural spray where a few drops on skin kill within minutes — knowledge only a naturalist/farm insider would command.
technical_detail.quote: A few drops of parathion on the skin can kill a person in minutes if they don't get treatment.

moral_ambiguity.value: Jim kills not from hatred but from a coherent, anguished ethic — he sees collectors and sprayers as murderers of innocent life, kills painlessly, and believes he executes justice for creatures no one else defends; Barbara, by contrast, is coldly self-interested, exploiting his sincerity.
moral_ambiguity.quote: "Vicious—that isn't true. They died painlessly. That's more than can be said for the countless helpless creatures they tortured and killed!"
